You are a code worker editing the freytag-forge repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files ONLY under the current working directory; NEVER create or edit anything under /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself (earlier workers wrongly wrote there; the check fails if you do). Do NOT git commit, do NOT git add -A, do NOT touch .git. Write short notes to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/astra-pipeline-eval-widen-notes/notes.md (create the directory).

OWNED FILES (all exist; edit only these): bench/pipeline_eval/model.py, bench/pipeline_eval/metrics.py, bench/pipeline_eval/runner.py, bench/pipeline_eval/__main__.py, bench/pipeline_eval/cases.json, tests/test_pipeline_eval.py, tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py. No production (storygame/) changes, no story data, no network, no model calls.

CONTEXT: Phase 3 of .plans/astra-implementation-plan.md. The harness and a first fixture exist (read all owned files first). Two defects must be fixed, and the fixture widened.

DEFECT 1 - brittle refusal checks. Today refused_move_prose cases use prose_includes ["cannot"] / ["can't"], a literal word match. Replace it:
 a) Add to Expectation a field prose_must_not_assert: tuple[str, ...] = (). Each entry is a plain-English description of an event the prose must NOT claim happened (for example "Kristin drives the truck away from the workstation"). It is never used as a substring match.
 b) score_turn gets an optional keyword argument claim_judge: Callable[[str, str], bool] | None = None, called as claim_judge(prose, claim), returning True when the prose asserts the claim. prose_correct is False if any claim is asserted. When prose_must_not_assert is set but claim_judge is None, prose_correct stays None (unchecked); NEVER fall back to word matching. run_arm and render_report accept and pass an optional claim_judge (default None), and the report prints "prose unchecked (no claim judge)" for such turns.
 c) A refusal is then shown by BOTH an expect.state naming the unmoved value (e.g. the truck still at its place) AND prose_must_not_assert. Remove every refusal-word prose_includes from the refusal cases. Keep prose_includes only where a name must appear (e.g. an NPC name).
 d) Tests with a stub claim_judge: asserting prose gives prose_correct False; non-asserting prose gives True; no judge gives None; the judge is called once per claim.

DEFECT 2 - unverified state keys. Cases use state keys like memory_card: with_kristin that nothing defines. Add to model.py a documented module constant STATE_VOCABULARY: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] mapping each state key a case may expect to its allowed values (e.g. memory_card: ("with_kristin", "not_with_kristin", "beneath_drawer"); use names matching real entities in data/stories/continuity-initiative: read world.yaml for entity ids, places and seats; keep it small and grounded). The docstring must say this is the contract arms report against and that mapping it to engine facts is a Phase 5 task. load_cases rejects an unknown state key or value. Add tests for rejection and acceptance, and have tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py assert every state key and value used in cases.json is in the vocabulary.

WIDEN the fixture: bench/pipeline_eval/cases.json must have, for EACH of the 14 existing categories (13 arch-review categories plus clarification_invariance), at least 3 DIAGNOSTIC and at least 3 HELD_OUT cases (ids category-d1..d3, category-h1..h3). Keep the existing cases (adapting the refusal ones as above). Vary the start state across cases within a category (different setup_facts, different scene where grounded, different save_load_after index) rather than only rewording. All ids must really exist in data/stories/continuity-initiative (reuse the real ones the existing cases and tests/test_1a_gap_pointer.py, tests/test_seating.py, tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py use; do not invent entities, facts or reveal ids). Player input per docs/player-input-guide.md (imperative, "my" possessives, no "do not"/"without"/"avoid", verb plus direct object, no non-events like "Wait."). Held-out commands share no exact string with any diagnostic command and use genuinely different wording. Update tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py: >=3 per split per category; existing grounding checks still hold; the vocabulary check; and a check that no case uses prose_includes with a refusal word (cannot, can't, unable, refuse).

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame, bench; print(storygame.__file__, bench.__file__)"` prints paths inside the cwd. Test: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_pipeline_eval.py tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py. CLI: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m bench.pipeline_eval report --cases bench/pipeline_eval/cases.json and the same with smoke. Ruff: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix bench/pipeline_eval tests/test_pipeline_eval.py tests/test_pipeline_eval_cases.py and -m ruff format on the same paths. Do not use uv. In notes.md list per category the case ids and what start state varies, and any category you could not widen with grounding (and why). Reply with the files changed.
tasks.verified: >=3 cases per split per category, refusal via injectable claim judge not word match, state keys validated against a vocabulary
